convergence_observation: Between-rep convergence is very high in every cell with two reps. E1: identical defect list, identical zero-dep decision with Framer Motion priced, identical derived-dirty model, and both reps used the phrase 'reward early, punish late'. E3: both sticky-track zero-dep, both rejected animation-timeline:scroll() on browser support, both split continuous CSS-var from discrete data-attribute channels, both used pathLength=1 to avoid getTotalLength(); act boundaries differ by 0.04. E4: both one shared viewport WebGL2 overlay synced to data-project-media rects, both rejected per-card canvases on the context-limit argument and R3F on the 'shader is identical either way' argument, both spotted that a page-wide canvas is what lets the open transition escape the card box. E5: both Canvas 2D + sprite atlas + React-free typed-array engine with WebGL as swappable escalation. E2: both identified animejs as v4 not v3, both chose the same two-nested-layer single-writer transform architecture, both used createScope mediaQueries with revert() cleanup. IMPLICATION FOR CRITERION A: the baseline is not merely near-ceiling, it is LOW-VARIANCE near-ceiling, so a three-rep median will have almost no spread and the 0.10-tolerance test becomes trivially easy to pass. The only cell with real discriminating power is E6.
